source.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations

record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests whether model neurons can serve as circuit units: it causally ablates extracted neuron sets and measures effects on target probabilities. It does not use attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The study measures grammatical concept circuits, not how many neuron poles have one or two human-named jobs, and does not test explanations on held-out activating examples. Its Qwen × Python ablation results bear on V5's broader neuron-as-circuit-units claim. Other reported results, including cross-model concept rankings, layer profiles, cross-language sharing, clustering, and linear-probe accuracy, do not measure the specific outcomes named by the claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: V5 is about attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons explaining its behaviour without a trained replacement model. This study builds none. It extracts thresholded concept-only neuron masks with its own method. Its zero-ablation test (§7.1) checks whether that decomposition is causally selective: a concept-versus-checker change in log P against a size-matched random null. It does not measure how much of the model's behaviour neuron-level circuits explain, and has no replacement-model comparison. The ablation is validation of the study's own method on neurons as units, so it is T4. The probe results (§7.2) show structure the neuron masks miss, but bear on no version directly. No other version (neuron-pole shares, InceptionV1, explanation scoring) is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, but secondary. The main conclusion is that the two models agree on which concepts get circuitry (ρ≈0.64–0.67) but differ on where and how those circuits are organised. Causal ablation covers only Qwen × Python: four concepts pass, two are marginal, Break fails, and small sets show no effect. The authors call the binary neuron decomposition 'correct but partial' because it misses sub-threshold distributed structure.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts concept-specific neuron masks and tests them with zero-ablation; it does not construct attribution graphs or measure reconstruction error.
record.method_sensitivity: The binarisation threshold changes circuit density and signal: ε = 0.001 gives trivially full circuits, ε = 0.1 gives near-zero concept-only fractions, and ε = 0.5 is used for structural signal. The consistency filter is inert for these dense models.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (Python), zero-ablating thresholded concept-only neuron sets dissociates concept from checker prompts beyond a size-matched null for 4 of 10 concepts. Two are marginal, Break fails, and sets under ~20 neurons show no effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-specific neuron sets found by contrastive thresholding are causally selective for some code-syntax concepts, but not reliably for all.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes decode concept vs checker at 97.6–99.7% at every layer, even where concept-only neuron sets are small and ablation has no effect. Probe-direction cosine and concept-only Jaccard correlate only moderately (r=0.645 at L20). The authors attribute this to distributed sub-threshold structure that the binary neuron view misses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-amplitude neuron masks give a correct but partial account; substantial concept information is distributed across sub-threshold neurons.

record.problems: Causal validation is limited to Qwen × Python, one of four model-language cells. It tests ablation effects rather than completeness of behavioral explanations or attribution-graph reconstruction. The authors also report that the binary method misses distributed sub-threshold structure.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-linked rows were omitted. Other results in §§4–7 were left out because they measure concept rankings, layer placement, cross-language sharing, clustering, or probe decodability rather than the outcomes named by the claim versions.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V5 labels are reversed here. The ablation validates the study's own extraction method and does not measure V5's construct (attribution graphs explaining behaviour without a replacement model). Its effect sizes are small (|Δ log P| ≤ 0.054), and they are not framed as explaining behaviour.

versions.untested_parts: The share of neuron poles with one or two main jobs and the share not yet understood.
Pole-level interpretability shares across models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, and trillion-parameter scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture and tool effects on interpretable-neuron shares, including the stated InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.

tranche.reason: Study builds its own thresholded concept-only neuron masks and validates them by zero-ablation and probes; no attribution graphs, replacement-model comparison or neuron-interpretability audit, so it bears on no version.

Causal test covers only Qwen x Python.
